newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, mulls Sumitomo news.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, mulls Sumitomo news.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer against a background of Sumitomo's reassurances it had no uncovered positions left, a sharp rise in U.S. housing starts in August, and expectations of a drop in LME stocks Friday.

Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said the information from Sumitomo lent support to the market, and the lack of surprises from Wednesday's Congressional hearings on banking and the Sumitomo crisis pacified some concerns.
"LME stocks are expected to fall Friday, continuing the downward trend," Raptopoulos said.
In August, U.S. housing starts, a major copper consuming sector, rose 4.5 percent to a rate of 1.525 million annually, the highest since March 1994.
COMEX went out 0.55 cent firmer at 90.20 cents, traded 90.95 to 88.80 cents. Spot September settled 0.75 cent higher at 91.55 cents.
LME cash to three-months contracts ended in slight contango while New York remained in backwardation.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said good demand in the U.S., helped by a domestic scrap shortage, and signs of Chinese rebuilding stocks, were supportive.
"Looking at the market over the next month, the physical market will give it an upside bias," said O'Neill.
